About the Position

This project investigates the mechanisms of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) repair using Drosophila and human cell models in Prof. Hansong Ma's laboratory.

OpportunityPhD Studentship: Mitochondrial DNA Repair
HostUniversity of Birmingham
LocationBirmingham, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingPartially Funded, stipend provided
Stipend£21,805/year (UKRI minimum stipend 2026/27)
Application Deadline24 October 2026
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Tuition Coverage to Check

The advertised package covers Home-rate tuition. It should not be treated as full international-fee funding: confirm your fee status and any overseas-fee difference with the university before accepting.

Basic Information

  • Full Project Title: Mitochondrial DNA Repair
  • Host Institution: University of Birmingham
  • Department: School of Biosciences
  • Supervisor: Prof. Hansong Ma
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 4 years
  • Start Date: 2027
  • Funding Type: funded at the Home-fee rate (Home UK students)
  • Stipend: UKRI rate (tax-free)
  • Tuition Fees: Covered at Home rate (international students must cover fee difference)
  • Eligibility: Home UK students (international applications welcome but must self-fund fee difference)
  • Application Deadline: 24 October 2026
  • Contact: h.ma.6@bham.ac.uk

Project Description

This project investigates the mechanisms of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) repair. Research will be conducted in Prof. Hansong Ma's laboratory, combining genetics, cell biology, and molecular biology approaches using Drosophila and human cell models to uncover the fundamental principles regulating mtDNA inheritance and stability.

Requirements

  • Strong academic background in molecular biology, genetics, or a related field

Contact

  • Email: h.ma.6@bham.ac.uk

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/research/birmingham-fly-facility/our-research/mitochondrial-dna-transmission-maintenance

Source: birmingham.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 24 October 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About University of Birmingham

The University of Birmingham is a public research university in Birmingham, England, and a Russell Group member. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study across engineering, medicine, science, business, humanities and social sciences. Research and teaching bring together different disciplines to investigate challenges affecting health, technology, communities and the environment.

Official website: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/

How to Apply

Email your CV and a cover letter outlining your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation to Prof. Hansong Ma (h.ma.6@bham.ac.uk).

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
